enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
1132 AM MDT Wed Oct 28 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION...


.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 1121 AM MDT Wed Oct 28 2026

 - Isolated thunderstorms possible in Hudspeth county today, 
   otherwise will be dry and quiet.

 - Showers with embedded thunderstorms expected areawide Thursday
   and into portions of Friday. Brief stretch of quiet weather for
   Halloween.

 - A potent upper level system will bring showers and
   thunderstorms to the area Sunday and into Monday. Increased
   flooding risk from thunderstorms. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1121 AM MDT Wed Oct 28 2026

Mostly calm and quiet weather in store today. Isolated thunderstorms 
possible this afternoon and early evening in Hudspeth and southern 
Otero counties. A slug of moisture will continue pushing north into 
our area on Thursday allowing PW values to reach a near record 
breaking value of around 1". A shortwave will act as the lifting 
mechanism for storms starting Thursday morning and persisting all 
day. Expecting showery activity with some embedded thunderstorms. 
The strongest storms will be capable of producing flash flooding. 
Storm chances persists into Friday. 

A brief break on Saturday but a much deeper trough will be the 
lifting mechanism for storms Sunday and into portions of Monday. 
Expect areawide rain chances Sunday. PWs will be well above normal 
again for this time of year on Sunday nearing around 0.9" to 1.0". 
Better forcing will increase the flooding threat. Winds will be 
slightly breezy Sunday becoming even breezier Monday. Moisture looks 
to quickly get shoved out behind this large upper trough Monday. 
Temperatures also look to take a dip too on Tuesday behind the low 
with lowland highs in the upper 60s and low 70s. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(18Z TAFS)
Issued at 1121 AM MDT Wed Oct 28 2026

Dry and quiet conditions today at terminals. Light winds generally 
AOB 10KT through the period and thickening high clouds. Rain showers 
will push in from the south Thursday morning. Expanding coverage of 
rain showers with embedded thunderstorms expected tomorrow 
afternoon. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 530 AM MDT Wed Oct 28 2026

Dry weather today with mostly sunny skies. SSW winds 5 to 10 mph 
this afternoon, leading to a few hours of Good vent rates.

Scattered rain showers developing Thursday afternoon will bring 
wetting precipitation to most of Gila and Lincoln NF through 
Friday. A few storms could be capable of heavy rain and flooding, 
especially within mountain canyons and creeks. Rain chances will 
continue through Sunday, with a stretch of drier weather next 
week. ERCs are very low at the moment, so no fire danger expected 
into early November.
